lessons.claim: A system with a driving protocol has to have its run split into **phases**, and 'is a steady state expected' differs per phase. trap-drag has four phases -- preheat, equilibrate, drag and relax -- and in the relax phase **the energy changing is the physics**, so running the drift check as it stands calls a discovery a warning (rule 7'). Phase.expect_steady=False turns the drift verdict off for that phase alone. Conversely a drift warning in the equilibration phase is real -- starting from a perfect-lattice IC makes ⟨U⟩ rise, so whether the preheat is sufficient has to be settled by measurement.
